title: IsA()
summary: Class check with inheritance: part:IsA("BasePart") is true for Part, MeshPart, WedgePart… Prefer it over ClassName comparisons whenever you mean 'is this kind of thing'.

details.heading: IsA vs ClassName
details.body: `inst.ClassName == "Part"` is exact-only. `inst:IsA("Part")` asks 'is this a Part or a subclass of Part?'. Everything IsA("Instance").

explanation.whatItIs: 'Are you this kind of thing, or a more specific version of it?'
explanation.whyItExists: Roblox classes form inheritance trees; gameplay usually cares about families (any BasePart), not exact species.
whenToUse: GUI element dispatch: IsA("TextButton") vs IsA("GuiButton")
whenNotToUse: When you genuinely need the exact class — ClassName ==
tips: IsA("BasePart") covers all physical parts — the most useful family check
Everything IsA("Instance") — useful as a generic validity test
commonMistakes: IsA on nil — guard first (`inst and inst:IsA(...)`)

examples.title: Family filtering
examples.code:
local parts = {}
for _, child in workspace.Map:GetChildren() do
    if child:IsA("BasePart") then          -- Part, MeshPart, WedgePart…
        table.insert(parts, child)
    elseif child:IsA("Model") then
        print("Found sub-model:", child.Name)
    end
end
